questions.question: Two resistors of 5 Ω and 15 Ω are connected in series to a battery of 10 V. How much will flow through the circuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **Series Connection**, resistors are connected end-to-end such that the same current flows through each resistor sequentially. The **Equivalent Resistance** (Rₑq) is calculated by the algebraic sum of individual resistances: Rₑq = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ.
 
• For the given circuit, the two resistors are **5 Ω** and **15 Ω**. Therefore, the total resistance is calculated as: Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 5 Ω + 15 Ω = **20 Ω**.
 
• **Ohm's Law** defines the relationship between voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R) in an ideal conductor, expressed by the formula: **V = I × R**.
 
• To find the current flowing through the circuit, we rearrange the formula to **I = V / R**. Substituting the given values: I = **10 V** / **20 Ω**.
 
• Performing the division, the current I = **0.5 A**. This indicates that a charge of 0.5 Coulombs passes through any point in the circuit every second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Series Circuit Characteristics**:

 
 
• The **Current (I)** remains uniform at every point in a series circuit; thus, 0.5 A flows through both the 5 Ω and 15 Ω resistors.
 
• The **Voltage (V)** across the battery is divided among the resistors. Using V = IR, the voltage drop across the 5 Ω resistor is 2.5 V, and across the 15 Ω resistor, it is 7.5 V, totaling the source 10 V.
 
• If one component in a series circuit **fails or breaks**, the entire circuit is interrupted, and current stops flowing completely.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Parallel Circuits**:
 
 
• In a **Parallel Connection**, the reciprocal of the total resistance is the sum of the reciprocals of individual resistances: 1/Rₚ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.
 
• Parallel circuits maintain the **same voltage** across all branches, but the total current is the sum of currents through each branch.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement**:
 
 
• **Resistance** is measured in **Ohms (Ω)**, named after Georg Simon Ohm.
 
• **Electric Current** is measured in **Amperes (A)**, representing the rate of flow of electric charge.
 
• **Potential Difference** is measured in **Volts (V)**, representing the work done to move a unit charge between two points.

questions.question:
Match the elements in Column I with their correct electron distribution in Column II according to the Bohr–Bury rules.

 
 

 Element
 <td style="width: 143px; text-align: center;"
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A–2, B–1, C–3, D–4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium (Na)** possesses an **atomic number** of **11**, which indicates it has 11 electrons in its neutral state. According to the **Bohr–Bury rules**, these are distributed as 2 in the **K-shell**, 8 in the **L-shell**, and the remaining 1 in the **M-shell**. ***Hence, Sodium (Na) matches with 2, 8, 1.***
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** has an **atomic number** of **12**. Its electron configuration is determined by filling the shells in increasing order of energy, resulting in 2 electrons in the **K-shell**, 8 in the **L-shell**, and 2 in the **M-shell**. ***Hence, Magnesium (Mg) matches with 2, 8, 2.***
 
• **Aluminium (Al)** is the element with **atomic number** **13**. Following the principle of maximum capacity and shell order, it houses 2 electrons in its innermost shell, 8 in the second, and 3 in the third shell. ***Hence, Aluminium (Al) matches with 2, 8, 3.***
 
• **Calcium (Ca)** has an **atomic number** of **20**. While the **M-shell** can hold up to 18 electrons, the **octet rule** dictates that the outermost shell cannot have more than 8 electrons; thus, after 8 electrons fill the **M-shell**, the next 2 enter the **N-shell**. ***Hence, Calcium (Ca) matches with 2, 8, 8, 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electronic Configuration Principles**:

 
 
• **2n² Formula**: This rule determines the maximum number of electrons a shell can hold, where **n** represents the **orbit number** or energy level (K=1, L=2, M=3, N=4).
 
• **Shell Capacities**: Based on the formula, the **K-shell** holds 2, **L-shell** holds 8, **M-shell** holds 18, and **N-shell** holds 32 electrons.
 
• **Valence Shell Stability**: The **outermost shell** of any atom cannot accommodate more than **8 electrons**, ensuring chemical stability as seen in **Noble Gases**.
 
• **Step-wise Filling**: Electrons do not occupy a new shell until the inner shells are completely filled, creating a structured **electronic arrangement**.
 
• **Valency**: The number of electrons in the **outermost shell** (valence electrons) determines the **valency** and reactivity of the element.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT explained by the Universal Law of Gravitation?

options.text: Falling of apples from a tree
Resistance offered by air to a moving object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Resistance offered by air to a moving object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Law of Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton**, states that every particle of matter in the universe attracts every other particle with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The **falling of apples** from a tree is caused by the gravitational attraction between the **Earth** and the apple, pulling the object toward the center of the planet.
 
• The **weight of objects** on Earth is a direct measure of the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on that object, calculated using the relationship **Weight = Mass × gravity**.
 
• The **formation of tides** in the Earth's oceans is a result of the gravitational pull exerted by the **Moon** and the **Sun**, which creates tidal bulges as the Earth rotates.
 
• **Air resistance**, or **drag**, is a **frictional force** exerted by air molecules against the motion of an object. This is a **contact force** dependent on the object's **velocity**, **surface area**, and **shape**, and is not explained by the principles of universal gravitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Constant (G)**

 
 
• It is a universal constant with a value of approximately 6.674 times 10⁻¹¹ { N m}² { kg}⁻² .
 
• Unlike the acceleration due to gravity (g), **G** remains constant throughout the universe.
 
 
 
• **Air Resistance (Fluid Friction)**
 
 
• It acts in the direction **opposite** to the relative motion of the object.
 
• In a **vacuum**, where air is absent, air resistance is zero, allowing objects of different masses to fall at the same rate.
 
• It is a **non-conservative force** because the energy spent overcoming it is dissipated as heat.
 
 
 
• **Tidal Forces**
 
 
• Tides are influenced more by the **Moon** than the Sun because of the Moon's proximity to Earth, despite the Sun's much larger mass.

questions.question: A farmer walks along the boundary of a square field with side 11 m, completing one round in 20 seconds. After walking for 3 minutes and 20 seconds, what is the magnitude of the displacement from his starting point?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The field is a **square** with a side length of **11 m**. The total **perimeter** of the field is 4 × 11 = **44 m**.
 
• The farmer completes one full round of the boundary in **20 seconds**.
 
• The total time spent walking is **3 minutes and 20 seconds**. To calculate this in seconds: (3 × 60) + 20 = **200 seconds**.
 
• The number of rounds completed is determined by dividing the **total time** by the **time per round**. Calculation: 200 / 20 = **10 full rounds**.
 
• Since the farmer completes exactly **10 rounds**, he returns precisely to the **starting point** on the boundary of the square field.
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity defined as the shortest straight-line distance between the **initial position** and the **final position**. Because the initial and final positions are the same, the displacement is **zero**. Hence, the magnitude of displacement is **0 m**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Distance vs. Displacement**:

 
 
• **Distance** is the total path length traveled, which in this case is 10 rounds × 44 m = **440 m**. Unlike displacement, it is a **scalar quantity** and cannot be zero if motion has occurred.
 
• **Displacement** depends only on the **endpoints** of the motion, not the path taken.
 
 
 
• **Vector Properties**:
 
 
• If the farmer had stopped after **10.5 rounds** (210 seconds), his displacement would be the **diagonal** of the square, calculated using the **Pythagoras theorem** as √(11² + 11²), which is approximately **15.56 m**.
 
• In **circular or closed-loop motion**, displacement is always zero if the object completes an **integer number** of revolutions or circuits.

questions.question: If the speed of light in a medium is 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s, its refractive index is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.33**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Refractive Index** (n) of a material is a dimensionless physical quantity that indicates the factor by which the **speed of light** is reduced inside the medium compared to its speed in a **vacuum**.
 
• The mathematical relationship is expressed by the formula **n = c / v**, where **c** represents the speed of light in a vacuum and **v** represents the speed of light in the given medium.
 
• The speed of light in a vacuum (c) is a universal physical constant valued at approximately **3 × 10⁸ m/s** (more precisely 299,792,458 m/s).
 
• Given that the speed of light in the medium is **2.25 × 10⁸ m/s**, the calculation is performed as follows: **n = (3 × 10⁸) / (2.25 × 10⁸)**.
 
• The **10⁸** terms in the numerator and denominator cancel out, leaving the ratio **3 / 2.25**. Converting the decimal, 2.25 is equivalent to 9/4, making the equation **3 / (9/4)**, which simplifies to **12/9** or **1.33**.
 
• A refractive index of **1.33** is a significant scientific value as it identifies the medium as **liquid water** at standard temperature and pressure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Optical Density and Refraction:**

 
 
• The refractive index is a measure of the **optical density** of a medium; a higher index implies light travels slower and bends more toward the **normal** when entering from a vacuum.
 
• **Snell's Law** (n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂) utilizes these indices to calculate the change in direction of light at an interface.
 
• The **Absolute Refractive Index** of a vacuum is exactly **1**, while for air, it is approximately **1.0003**, often rounded to 1 for basic physics calculations.
 
• Other common materials include **Crown Glass** (n ≈ 1.52), **Flint Glass** (n ≈ 1.66), and **Diamond**, which has a very high index of **2.42**, contributing to its extreme dispersion and brilliance.
 
• The refractive index can also depend on the **wavelength** of light, a phenomenon known as **dispersion**, which causes the separation of white light into a spectrum when passing through a prism.

questions.question: Which of the following is correct for substitution reaction?

options.text: A reaction where atoms or groups in a molecule are replaced by another atom or group.
A reaction where a compound breaks down into simpler substances.
A reaction where two compounds combine to form one.
A reaction where hydrogen is added to a compound.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A reaction where atoms or groups in a molecule are replaced by another atom or group.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **substitution reaction** is a fundamental chemical process where one **atom** or a **functional group** in a molecule is replaced by a different atom or group without changing the basic **carbon skeleton**.
 
• These reactions are primary characteristics of **saturated hydrocarbons** (alkanes) and **aromatic compounds** (like benzene) because these molecules lack **multiple bonds** where addition could occur.
 
• In **alkanes**, substitution usually involves the replacement of **hydrogen atoms** by **halogens** (Chlorine, Bromine, or Iodine) in the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) light** or high temperatures.
 
• The general representation of a simple substitution is **A-B + C → A-C + B**, where **C** displaces **B** from the original molecule.
 
• For example, in the **chlorination of methane** (CH₄), a chlorine atom replaces a hydrogen atom to produce **chloromethane** (CH₃Cl) and **hydrogen chloride** (HCl).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition Reaction**:

 
 
• Involves a single **chemical compound** breaking down into two or more simpler substances or **elements**.
 
• Usually requires an energy input in the form of **heat** (thermal), **light** (photolysis), or **electricity** (electrolysis).
 
 
 
• **Combination Reaction**:
 
 
• Occurs when two or more **reactants** (elements or compounds) unite to form a single, more complex **product**.
 
• Commonly referred to as a **synthesis reaction**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogenation**:
 
 
• A specific type of **addition reaction** where **hydrogen** (H₂) is added across the **double or triple bonds** of **unsaturated hydrocarbons**.
 
• Typically requires catalysts like **Nickel (Ni)**, **Palladium (Pd)**, or **Platinum (Pt)**.

questions.question: A wire has a resistance of 10 Ω. If it is stretched to three times its original length (volume remaining constant), its new resistance will be _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**90 omega**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Electrical Resistance** of a conductor is determined by the formula **R = ρ × (L / A)**, where ρ (rho) represents the **Resistivity** of the material, L is the **Length**, and A is the **Cross-sectional Area**.
 
• When a wire is stretched, its physical dimensions change, but its **Total Volume** remains constant. The volume (V) is calculated as the product of the cross-sectional area and the length (**V = A × L**).
 
• In this scenario, the wire is stretched to **three times** its original length (L' = 3L). Because the volume is constant (V = A × L = A' × 3L), the new cross-sectional area (A') must decrease to **one-third** of the original area (A' = A / 3).
 
• Substituting the new dimensions into the resistance formula, the new resistance (R') is calculated as: **R' = ρ × (3L / (A / 3))**. This simplifies to **R' = 9 × (ρ × L / A)**, which is **9 × R**.
 
• Given the initial resistance is **10 omega**, the new resistance becomes **9 × 10 = 90 omega**. This demonstrates that for a constant volume, resistance varies with the **Square of the Length** (R ∝ L²).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistivity (ρ):**

 
 
• It is an **Intrinsic Property** of the material, meaning it depends only on the nature of the substance and its **Temperature**, not on the shape or size.
 
• While **Resistance** increases nine-fold during stretching, the **Resistivity** remains unchanged as long as the material and temperature are constant.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:**
 
 
• **Length:** Doubling the length by adding another wire (without stretching) only doubles the resistance because the area remains constant.
 
• **Area:** Increasing the thickness (area) reduces resistance, which is why **Thicker Wires** are used for high-current applications to minimize power loss.
 
• **Temperature:** For most **Metallic Conductors**, resistance increases linearly with temperature due to increased electron-ion collisions.

questions.question: Which characteristic best describes parenchyma?

options.text: Living cells with thin walls, capable of division in young tissues.
Dead at maturity with thick secondary walls.
Cells arranged in a single layer with guarding function.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Living cells with thin walls, capable of division in young tissues**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parenchyma** is the most fundamental and abundant type of **simple permanent tissue**, forming the major part of the plant ground tissue system in roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• These are **living cells** at maturity, characterized by a functional **protoplast**, a prominent nucleus, and a large central **vacuole** used for storage and maintaining **turgor pressure**.
 
• The cells possess **thin primary cell walls** primarily composed of **cellulose** and hemicellulose, which lack **lignification**, allowing for flexibility and metabolic activity.
 
• A critical feature of parenchyma is its **meristematic potential**; in **young tissues** or upon injury, these cells can regain the ability for **cell division**, facilitating **wound healing** and regeneration.
 
• Structurally, they are often **isodiametric** (spherical or polygonal) with thin walls and prominent **intercellular spaces** that enable efficient **gas exchange** within the plant body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collenchyma (Option 1)**:

 
 
• These are living cells with **asymmetric primary wall thickenings**, specifically at the corners, due to **pectin** and cellulose deposition.
 
• They provide **mechanical support** and flexibility, allowing young plant organs like the **petiole** to **bend without breaking**.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma (Option 3)**:
 
 
• These cells are typically **dead at maturity** and characterized by extremely thick **secondary walls** reinforced with **lignin**.
 
• They provide the primary **structural rigidity** and mechanical strength to mature plant parts like **seeds** and vascular bundles.
 
 
 
• **Epidermis (Option 4)**:
 
 
• This is the outermost **single layer** of cells covering the entire plant body.
 
• It performs a **guarding function**, protecting against mechanical injury and regulating **transpiration** through specialized structures like **stomata**.

questions.question: An object has a mass of 12 kg and moves with a constant speed of 8 m/s. How much kinetic energy does it have?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**384 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy** is defined as the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It represents the work needed to accelerate a body of a given mass from rest to its stated velocity.
 
• The fundamental formula for calculating **Translational Kinetic Energy** is given by: K.E. = (1)/(2) mv² .
 
• From the problem statement, we have the following data:
 
 
• **Mass (m)** = **12 kg**.
 
• **Constant Speed (v)** = **8 m/s**.
 
 
 
• By substituting these values into the energy equation: K.E. = (1)/(2) times 12 times (8)² .
 
• Calculating the square of the velocity first: 8 × 8 = **64**.
 
• Continuing the calculation: 0.5 × 12 × 64 = 6 × 64 = **384**.
 
• The resulting value for the kinetic energy is **384 Joules (J)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relationship with Variables**:

 
 
• **Mass**: Kinetic energy is **linearly proportional** to the mass. If the mass of the object is doubled, the energy doubles.
 
• **Velocity**: Kinetic energy is proportional to the **square of the velocity**. This means if the speed is doubled, the energy increases by a factor of four.
 
 
 
• **SI Units**: The standard **International System of Units (SI)** unit for energy is the **Joule (J)**. One Joule is defined as 1 **kg·m²/s²**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: Kinetic energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it only has magnitude and no direction. Unlike **velocity** or **momentum**, the direction of travel does not affect the total energy value.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the change in its **kinetic energy**.

questions.question: After fertilisation in humans, where does the growth and development of the embryo mainly occur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uterus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **uterus**, also known as the **womb**, is a hollow, thick-walled, pear-shaped muscular organ located in the female pelvic cavity between the bladder and the rectum.
 
• After **fertilisation** occurs in the fallopian tube, the resulting **zygote** undergoes multiple cell divisions to become a **blastocyst**, which then travels to the uterus for **implantation**.
 
• **Implantation** typically occurs **6 to 10 days** after fertilisation, where the embryo embeds itself into the **endometrium**, the vascularized inner lining of the uterine wall.
 
• The uterus is the primary site for **gestation**, providing a protective environment and necessary physiological support for the **embryo** to develop into a **fetus** over a period of approximately **280 days** or **40 weeks**.
 
• During pregnancy, the **placenta** develops within the uterus to facilitate the exchange of **oxygen**, **nutrients**, and **antibodies** from the mother to the developing fetus while removing metabolic waste products.
 
• The muscular layer of the uterus, the **myometrium**, possesses the unique ability to expand significantly during pregnancy and contract powerfully during **parturition** (childbirth).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fallopian Tube**

 
 
• These are narrow tubes that serve as the pathway for the **ovum** to travel from the ovary to the uterus and are the specific site where **sperm** meets the egg for **fertilisation**, usually in the **ampulla** region.
 
 
 
• **Ovary**
 
 
• The primary female reproductive organs (gonads) responsible for the production of **oocytes** (eggs) and the secretion of key reproductive hormones, including **estrogen** and **progesterone**.
 
 
 
• **Vagina**
 
 
• An elastic, muscular canal that connects the **cervix** to the outside of the body; it serves as the **birth canal** during delivery and the site for the deposition of **semen** during intercourse.

questions.question: The far point of a myopic person is 80 cm in front of the eye. Assuming the far point for normal vision is infinity, what is the required power (P) of the corrective lens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-1.25 D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Myopia**, commonly referred to as **nearsightedness**, is a vision condition where close objects appear clear, but distant objects are blurry. This occurs when the **eyeball** is too long or the **cornea** is too curved, causing light to focus in front of the **retina**.
 
• To correct myopia, a **concave lens** (diverging lens) is required. This lens diverges incoming light rays so that they appear to originate from the person's actual **far point**, effectively moving the image onto the **retina**.
 
• The **lens formula** is expressed as: 1/f = 1/v − 1/u. For a myopic eye to see distant objects, the object is assumed to be at **infinity** (u = −∞), and the image must be formed at the person's far point (v = **−80 cm** or **−0.8 m**).
 
• Substituting these values into the formula: 1/f = 1/(−80) − 1/(−∞). Since 1/∞ is 0, we find that the **focal length (f)** is equal to the far point, which is **−80 cm**.
 
• The **Power (P)** of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length in **meters** (P = 1/f). Converting the focal length, f = −0.8 m. Therefore, P = 1 / (−0.8) = **−1.25 Dioptres (D)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Lens Properties**:

 
 
• These lenses are **thinner at the center** and thicker at the edges.
 
• They always possess a **negative focal length**, which results in a **negative power** value in prescriptions.
 
 
 
• **Dioptre (D)**:
 
 
• It is the **standard unit** of measurement for the optical power of a lens or curved mirror.
 
• A power of **+1.25 D** would indicate a **convex lens**, used for correcting **Hypermetropia** (farsightedness), where the image forms behind the retina.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of uniform circular motion?

options.text: Moon revolving around the Earth in a circular orbit
A roller coaster on a loop
A racing car on a curved track slowing down
A yo-yo being swung in a vertical circle at changing speed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moon revolving around the Earth in a circular orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform circular motion** is defined as the motion of an object traveling at a **constant speed** along a circular path.
 
• In this type of motion, while the **magnitude of velocity** (speed) remains unchanged, the **direction of motion** changes continuously at every point on the path.
 
• The **Moon revolving around the Earth** is a prime example because it maintains a nearly constant speed as it covers its orbit, driven by the **Earth’s gravitational pull**.
 
• The **gravitational force** acts as the **centripetal force**, which is always directed toward the center of the orbit, perpendicular to the object's velocity.
 
• Since the direction changes at every instant, the object is said to have **centripetal acceleration**, even though the speed is uniform.
 
• This motion is also **periodic**, meaning the Moon takes the same amount of time to complete one full revolution around the Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The motion of an athlete running along a circular path with constant speed is an example of accelerated motion because __________.

options.text: The direction of motion changes continuously
The mass of the athlete is constant
A constant external force is applied

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The direction of motion changes continuously**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Velocity** is defined as a **vector quantity**, which means it possesses both **magnitude (speed)** and a specific **direction** of motion.
 
• **Acceleration** is the rate of change of **velocity** over time. For an object to accelerate, there must be a change in its speed, its **direction**, or both.
 
• In the case of an athlete running on a **circular path**, even if the **speed** remains constant, the **direction** of their motion is forced to change at every infinitesimal point along the curve to maintain the circular trajectory.
 
• Since the **direction** is changing continuously, the **velocity vector** is not constant. This change in velocity per unit of time constitutes **accelerated motion**.
 
• This specific form of motion is known as **Uniform Circular Motion**, where the magnitude of velocity (speed) is fixed, but the motion is still categorized as accelerated due to the directional shift.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• The acceleration acting on the athlete is directed towards the **center of the circular path** and is perpendicular to the **velocity vector**.
 
• The formula for this acceleration is a = v²/r, where **v** is the constant speed and **r** is the radius of the track.
 
 
 
• **Tangential Velocity**:
 
 
• At any given moment, the athlete's **velocity vector** is **tangent** to the circle. If the athlete were to suddenly lose grip or stop turning, they would move in a straight line along this tangent.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal Force**:
 
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law** (F = ma), this acceleration requires a **centripetal force** acting towards the center, which in this case is provided by the **friction** between the athlete's shoes and the track.

questions.question: What causes only the animal cell to burst when both plant and animal cells are placed in pure water?

options.text: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall.
Animal cells have a thicker membrane.
Plant cells can actively pump out water.
Osmosis occurs only in animal cells.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plant cells have a rigid cell wall.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When cells are placed in **pure water**, which acts as a **hypotonic solution**, water molecules move into the cells through the process of **osmosis** to balance solute concentrations.
 
• **Animal cells** are surrounded only by a thin, flexible **plasma membrane**. As water enters, the internal **osmotic pressure** increases, causing the cell to swell until the membrane ruptures, a process known as **osmotic lysis**.
 
• **Plant cells** contain a tough, **rigid cell wall** located outside the plasma membrane, primarily composed of **cellulose**, which provides significant mechanical strength.
 
• As water enters the **plant cell**, the **large central vacuole** fills up and pushes the **protoplast** against the cell wall, generating **turgor pressure**.
 
• The **rigid cell wall** exerts an equal and opposite **wall pressure** against the expanding cytoplasm, which limits further water intake and prevents the cell from **bursting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypotonic Solution**

 
 
• A solution where the **solute concentration** is lower than that inside the cell, leading to a net **influx of water**.
 
 
 
• **Turgidity**
 
 
• The state of being **turgid** helps plants maintain their **structural integrity** and keep leaves upright for maximum **sunlight absorption**.
 
 
 
• **Plasmolysis**
 
 
• Occurs when a plant cell is placed in a **hypertonic solution**, causing water to leave the cell and the **cell membrane** to shrink away from the **cell wall**.
 
 
 
• **Cellulose**
 
 
• A **polysaccharide** that forms the primary structural component of the **green plant cell wall**, providing the **tensile strength** required to withstand internal pressure.

• This increased **surface area** allows for a much larger number of **electron transport chain (ETC)** complexes and **ATP synthase** enzymes to be embedded in the membrane.
 
• A greater concentration of these proteins enables more efficient **oxidative phosphorylation**, leading to a higher rate of **ATP generation** to meet the metabolic demands of the cell.
 
• The structure-to-function relationship of the **cristae** is a classic biological example of maximizing **efficiency** through **geometric optimization**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondrial Anatomy**:

 
 
• **Outer Membrane**: A smooth phospholipid bilayer containing **porins** that make it permeable to small molecules and ions.

• **Mitochondrial Matrix**: The dense internal fluid containing **circular DNA**, **70S ribosomes**, and enzymes for the **TCA (Krebs) cycle**.

• **Cell Wall Thickness**: This term refers to the structural layer outside the **plasma membrane** in plants (cellulose), fungi (chitin), and bacteria (peptidoglycan); mitochondria do not possess cell walls.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the unit mass of a molecule of water ( {H}₂{O} )?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **molecular mass** of a compound is the sum of the **atomic masses** of all the constituent atoms present in a single molecule of that substance.
 
• The chemical formula for water is **H₂O**, indicating it contains two atoms of **Hydrogen** and one atom of **Oxygen**.
 
• The **atomic mass** of **Hydrogen (H)** is approximately **1 u**, and the **atomic mass** of **Oxygen (O)** is approximately **16 u**.
 
• To find the total mass, the calculation is performed as: (2 × 1 u) + (1 × 16 u) = 2 u + 16 u = **18 u**.
 
• The unit **u** stands for the **unified atomic mass unit**, which is the standard unit for expressing masses at the atomic scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unified Atomic Mass Unit (u)**:

 
 
• It is defined as a mass exactly equal to **one-twelfth (1/12th)** of the mass of one **Carbon-12** atom.
 
• This unit replaced the older **amu** (atomic mass unit) to provide a more precise international standard.
 
 
 
• **Molar Mass Comparison**:
 
 
• While molecular mass is 18 u (mass of one molecule), the **molar mass** of water is **18 g/mol**.
 
• This represents the mass of one mole of water molecules, which equals **6.022 × 10²³** molecules (**Avogadro number**).
 
 
 
• **Heavy Water (D₂O)**:
 
 
• If Hydrogen is replaced by its isotope **Deuterium** (which has an atomic mass of 2 u), the resulting substance is called **Heavy Water**.
 
• The molecular mass of **D₂O** is (2 × 2 u) + 16 u = **20 u**, which is frequently used as a moderator in **nuclear reactors**.

questions.question: Which condition is required for methane to undergo a substitution reaction with chlorine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Methane** (CH₄) is a **saturated hydrocarbon** belonging to the **alkane** family, characterized by single covalent bonds between carbon and hydrogen atoms.
 
• Alkanes are generally **inert** at room temperature and do not react with reagents like chlorine in the dark; however, they undergo **substitution reactions** under specific conditions.
 
• The reaction between **methane** and **chlorine** is a **photochemical reaction** that requires the presence of **Sunlight** or **Ultraviolet (UV) radiation** to proceed.
 
• Light energy provides the necessary **activation energy** to initiate **homolytic fission** of the chlorine-chlorine bond, where the shared pair of electrons is split equally between the two atoms.
 
• This fission creates highly reactive **chlorine free radicals**, which are essential intermediates that attack the stable methane molecules to begin the substitution process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Free Radical Substitution Mechanism**:

 
 
• **Initiation**: The **UV light** photons break the Cl-Cl bond: Cl₂ xrightarrow{hnu} 2Clbullet .
 
• **Propagation**: A **chlorine radical** reacts with methane to form **hydrogen chloride** (HCl) and a **methyl radical** (CH₃•). This methyl radical then reacts with another chlorine molecule to produce **chloromethane** (CH₃Cl).
 
• **Termination**: The reaction ends when two radicals combine to form a stable molecule, such as **dichloromethane**, ethane, or more chloromethane.
 
 
 
• **Successive Substitution**:
 
 
• If chlorine is provided in excess, the reaction continues through a **chain reaction**, successively replacing all hydrogen atoms to form **dichloromethane** (CH₂Cl₂), **trichloromethane** (CHCl₃ or **chloroform**), and finally **tetrachloromethane** (CCl₄ or **carbon tetrachloride**).
 
 
 
• **Reactivity of Alkanes**: Alkanes are often termed **paraffins** (from Latin 'parum affinis' meaning 'little affinity') because they exhibit low chemical reactivity toward most laboratory reagents due to the high stability of **C-H** and **C-C** sigma bonds.

__
 
• Pure water undergoes a process known as **self-ionization** or **auto-ionization**, where a tiny fraction of water molecules act as both an acid and a base to produce ions.
 
• The chemical equilibrium for this reversible reaction is represented as: **H₂O + H₂O ↔ H₃O⁺ + OH−**, or more simply as **H₂O ↔ H⁺ + OH−**.
 
• The equilibrium constant for this dissociation is called the **ionic product of water**, symbolized as **Kw**.
 
• At a standard temperature of **25°C** (or 298 K), the value of **Kw** is experimentally determined to be exactly **1.0 × 10−¹⁴ mol²/L²**.
 
• In pure water, every single dissociation event produces one **hydrogen ion (H⁺)** and one **hydroxide ion (OH−)**, ensuring their concentrations remain perfectly equal: **[H⁺] = [OH−]**.
 
• By substituting this equality into the expression **Kw = [H⁺] × [OH−]**, we obtain the equation **1.0 × 10−¹⁴ = [H⁺]²**.
 
• Taking the square root of both sides leads to the concentration of **[H⁺] = 1.0 × 10−⁷ moles per liter (M)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **pH Scale and Neutrality**:

 
 
• The **pH** is the negative base-10 logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration: **pH = −log[H⁺]**.
 
• For pure water at **25°C**, the pH is **−log(10−⁷) = 7**, defining the neutral point on the scale.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Dependence**:
 
 
• The **auto-ionization** of water is an **endothermic process**. According to **Le Chatelier's Principle**, increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium to the right.
 
• At temperatures higher than **25°C**, **Kw** increases, resulting in a higher concentration of **H⁺** ions and a neutral pH lower than 7.
 
 
 
• **Molarity (M)**:
 
 
• Molarity is a unit of concentration expressing the number of **moles of solute** per **liter of solution**.
 
• Even in highly acidic or basic solutions, the product of **[H⁺]** and **[OH−]** always equals **Kw** at that specific temperature.

questions.question: A scientist observed that an iron railing near the sea corroded faster than the same type of railing in a dry city. What could the main reason be?

options.text: The city air has less oxygen, preventing rust.
The sea air is more humid, diluting the rusting process.
The iron near the sea is exposed to more sunlight.
Sea air contains salt and moisture, which accelerates rusting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sea air contains salt and moisture, which accelerates rusting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rusting** is an oxidative process where **iron** reacts with **oxygen** and **moisture** (water) to form **hydrated iron (III) oxide**. For this chemical reaction to occur effectively, both air and water must be present simultaneously on the metal surface.
 
• The environment near the sea is characterized by high **humidity**, meaning the air contains a high concentration of water vapor. This provides the necessary **moisture** for the corrosion process to begin.
 
• **Sea air** also carries tiny particles of **salt**, primarily **sodium chloride (NaCl)**. Salt acts as a powerful **electrolyte** when dissolved in the moisture film on the iron railing.
 
• As an electrolyte, salt increases the **electrical conductivity** of the water, which facilitates the flow of ions between the **anodic** and **cathodic** areas on the metal surface. This electrochemical enhancement significantly **accelerates** the rate of iron degradation compared to the **dry air** found in inland cities.
 
• In a **dry city**, the lack of sufficient moisture acts as a limiting factor, meaning the oxidation process occurs at a negligible or much slower rate, even if oxygen is abundant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical Formulation of Rust**:

 
 
• The overall chemical reaction for rusting can be expressed as: 4Fe + 3O₂ + xH₂O rightarrow 2Fe₂O₃ · xH₂O .
 
• The resulting product is a reddish-brown, **porous**, and flaky substance that does not stick to the metal, allowing further layers of iron to be exposed and corroded.
 
 
 
• **Methods of Prevention**:
 
 
• **Galvanization**: This involves coating the iron or steel with a thin layer of **zinc**. Zinc is more reactive than iron and acts as a **sacrificial anode**, corroding itself to protect the underlying iron.
 
• **Alloying**: Mixing iron with elements like **chromium** and **nickel** creates **stainless steel**. Chromium forms a thin, invisible layer of **chromium oxide** on the surface, which prevents further oxygen penetration.
 
• **Barrier Protection**: Methods such as **painting**, **greasing**, or **oiling** create a physical shield that blocks moisture and air from reaching the iron surface.

questions.question: Why is vegetative propagation useful for agriculture purposes?

options.text: It requires seeds for every generation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It produces identical plants rapidly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vegetative propagation** is a type of **asexual reproduction** in which new plants are produced from vegetative parts like **roots, stems, and leaves**, rather than through flowers or seeds.
 
• Since the process involves only **mitotic cell division** and a single parent, the resulting offspring are **genetically identical clones**, ensuring that **desirable characteristics** of the parent plant are preserved exactly in the next generation.
 
• This method allows for a much **faster rate of reproduction** compared to sexual reproduction, as it bypasses the time-consuming stages of **pollination, fertilization, and seed germination**.
 
• It is particularly useful for **agricultural purposes** when dealing with plants that have **lost the capacity to produce viable seeds**, such as commercial varieties of **banana, orange, rose, and jasmine**.
 
• Farmers can maintain **uniformity in crop quality** and harvest times, which is essential for large-scale **commercial farming** and food supply chain management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Techniques**:

 
 
• **Cutting**: A part of the stem or root is placed in moist soil to grow (e.g., **Sugarcane**).
 
• **Layering**: A branch is lowered to the ground and covered with soil to develop roots while still attached to the parent (e.g., **Jasmine**).
 
• **Grafting**: Joining a **scion** (top part) with a **stock** (rooted part) to combine traits (e.g., **Mango**).
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options**:
 
 
• **Genetic Variation**: Unlike sexual reproduction, vegetative propagation results in **low genetic diversity**, which can be a disadvantage if the environment changes or a new **pathogen** emerges.
 
• **Disease Prevention**: This method does **not prevent diseases naturally**; in fact, if the parent plant is infected with a **virus**, the clones will also carry that same infection.

questions.question: How much work is required to move a charge of 3 C between two points that have a potential difference of 15 V?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**45 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Electric Potential Difference** (V) between two points in an electrical circuit is defined as the amount of **Work Done** (W) in moving a unit **Electric Charge** (Q) from one point to another.
 
• The fundamental relationship between these physical quantities is mathematically expressed by the formula: **Work Done (W) = Potential Difference (V) × Charge (Q)**.
 
• According to the problem statement, the magnitude of the **Charge (Q)** to be moved is **3 C** (Coulombs).
 
• The **Potential Difference (V)** maintained between the two specific points in the circuit is **15 V** (Volts).
 
• By applying the values to the formula, we calculate the work as follows: **W = 15 V × 3 C**, which results in a value of **45 J**.
 
• Therefore, the total amount of energy expended or work required to transport the charge is exactly **45 Joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Standard International (SI) Units**:

 
 
• **Joule (J)**: Named after **James Prescott Joule**, it is the SI unit of **Work** and **Energy**. One Joule is equal to the work done by a force of one **Newton** acting through a distance of one meter.
 
• **Volt (V)**: Named after **Alessandro Volta**, it is the SI unit for **Electric Potential**. One Volt is defined as the consumption of one Joule of energy per Coulomb of charge (1 V = 1 J/C).
 
• **Coulomb (C)**: Named after **Charles-Augustin de Coulomb**, it is the SI unit of **Electric Charge**. It is defined as the quantity of electricity transported in one second by a current of one **Ampere**.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Electric Potential**: It represents the **Potential Energy** per unit charge. When a charge moves through a potential difference, its electrostatic potential energy changes, which is reflected as the work done on or by the charge.
 
• **Related Formulas**: In broader electrical physics, potential difference is also linked to **Current (I)** and **Resistance (R)** through **Ohm's Law** (V = I × R) and to **Power (P)** (P = V × I).

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents a diatomic element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **diatomic element** consists of molecules made up of exactly **two atoms** of the **same chemical element** bonded together.
 
• **Hydrogen** exists naturally as a **diatomic molecule**, represented by the chemical formula **H₂**, where two hydrogen atoms are joined by a **single covalent bond**.
 
• There are seven elements that naturally exist as **homonuclear diatomic molecules** under standard temperature and pressure: **Hydrogen (H₂)**, **Nitrogen (N₂)**, **Oxygen (O₂)**, **Fluorine (F₂)**, **Chlorine (Cl₂)**, **Bromine (Br₂)**, and **Iodine (I₂)**.
 
• The subscript 2 in **H₂** indicates the presence of two atoms, making it the correct molecular representation of the element in its stable state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **He (Helium)**:

 
 
• Helium is a **Noble Gas** (Group 18) and is **monatomic**, meaning it exists as single, stable atoms.
 
 
 
• **CO (Carbon Monoxide)**:
 
 
• While CO consists of two atoms, it is a **compound** (heteronuclear molecule) rather than an element because it contains atoms of two different elements: **Carbon** and **Oxygen**.
 
 
 
• **H (Hydrogen Atom)**:
 
 
• This symbol represents a single **Hydrogen atom** or the element symbol itself, but it does not represent the stable **molecular form** of the element as found in nature.

questions.question: How much energy will be available to the tertiary consumer if a food chain begins with 5000 J of energy at the producer level?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The flow of energy in an ecosystem is governed by the **10 percent Law**, which was formulated by **Raymond Lindeman** in **1942**. This principle states that during the transfer of organic food energy from one **trophic level** to the next, only about **10 percent** of the energy is stored as flesh.
 
• Starting at the **Producer level** (the first trophic level) with an initial energy of **5000 J**, the energy available to the next level is calculated by taking 10 percent of the preceding level's energy.
 
• The **Primary Consumer** (second trophic level) receives 10 percent of 5000 J, which is 5000 × 0.10 = **500 J**.
 
• The **Secondary Consumer** (third trophic level) receives 10 percent of the energy from the primary consumer, which is 500 × 0.10 = **50 J**.
 
• The **Tertiary Consumer** (fourth trophic level) receives 10 percent of the energy from the secondary consumer, which is 50 × 0.10 = **5 J**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**:

 
 
• **Producers**: These are **autotrophs**, primarily **green plants**, that capture **solar energy** to produce food through **photosynthesis**. They form the base of the energy pyramid.
 
• **Consumers**: These are **heterotrophs** that depend on producers for energy. They include **herbivores** (Primary), **carnivores** (Secondary), and **apex predators** (Tertiary).
 
• **Energy Dissipation**: Approximately **90 percent** of energy is lost at each step, mainly as **heat** during **respiration** and metabolic processes. This massive energy loss limits the length of **food chains** to typically 4 or 5 levels.
 
• **Unidirectional Flow**: Unlike nutrients, which cycle through the ecosystem, the **flow of energy** is always **unidirectional**, moving from lower to higher trophic levels and eventually dissipating into the environment.

questions.question: The principal focus of a concave mirror is:

options.text: A point on the mirror where all rays meet
The center of curvature of the mirror
The point where rays parallel to the principal axis converge after reflection

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The point where rays parallel to the principal axis converge after reflection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a type of **spherical mirror** whose reflecting surface is curved inwards, toward the center of the sphere. It is commonly referred to as a **converging mirror** because it collects light rays and brings them together.
 
• The **principal focus (F)** is a specific point located on the **principal axis** of the mirror. When a beam of light consisting of rays **parallel** to the principal axis strikes the concave mirror, the rays follow the **laws of reflection** and intersect at this point.
 
• In the case of a concave mirror, the light rays actually meet at the focus, making it a **real focus**. This property allows the mirror to be used in devices like **solar furnaces** to concentrate heat at a single point.
 
• The position of the **principal focus** is exactly halfway between the **pole (P)** and the **center of curvature (C)** for mirrors with small apertures.
 
• The distance between the **pole** and the **principal focus** is defined as the **focal length (f)** of the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Center of Curvature (C)**:

 
 
• This is the **center of the hollow sphere** of glass of which the mirror was originally a part. It is situated in front of the reflecting surface of a **concave mirror**.
 
 
 
• **Pole (P)**:
 
 
• The **geometric center** or the midpoint of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called the pole. It lies on the surface of the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature (R)**:
 
 
• The distance from the **pole** to the **center of curvature**. In spherical mirrors of small aperture, the radius of curvature is found to be **twice the focal length**, represented by the formula **R = 2f**.
 
 
 
• **Principal Axis**:
 
 
• A horizontal straight line that passes through both the **pole** and the **center of curvature**, acting as the reference line for object and image distances.
